newsitem.title: USA: PG&E says Calif hydro plant may need new equipment.
newsitem.headline: PG&E says Calif hydro plant may need new equipment.

text.p: Pacific Gas and Electric Co may need to purchase equipment from outside its own system in order to repair its 1,212 megawatt (MW) Helms hydroelectric plant, a company spokeswoman said Friday.
"We hope to determine when and where parts will need to be brought in by early next week," at which time a schedule for restarting the plant may be set, she said.

The Helms plant, near Fresno, Calif., on the Kings River, is a pumped storage facility that consumes energy at night, during low-power demand hours, to move water uphill so it can be released to flow through turbines during the day.
Since so few of those types of plants exist, PG&E may need to seek replacement parts from other companies.
The Helms plant was shut Feb 1 when a transformer bank for one of the projects three 404 MW generators failed, causing a fire which damaged all three units.
